notes: §1985:VII.2.3.2 prints the sequential file control entry: SELECT [OPTIONAL] file-name-1, a required ASSIGN with a list of 'implementor-name-1' or literal-1, then the optional RESERVE, [ORGANIZATION IS] SEQUENTIAL, 'PADDING CHARACTER IS', RECORD DELIMITER, ACCESS 'MODE IS' SEQUENTIAL and FILE STATUS clauses and a period, in any order after SELECT (§1985:VII.2.3.3 SR1). The superset rules fileControlClauseGroup and fileControlClauses parse them with every optional word omitted or written, and the 1985 shape is restored after the parse: Screen over RequiredClauses refuses an entry without ASSIGN (COBOL5701), BindFileControl refuses ACCESS MODE RANDOM or DYNAMIC on a sequential file (COBOL1858), Screen over the EntryClauses rows refuses RECORD KEY, RELATIVE KEY and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY (COBOL0863), ScreenClauseRepetition a repeated clause (COBOL2423), VisitUnrecognizedClause any other word (COBOL1970), IntegerOperandPass RESERVE 0 (COBOL2386), and the VersionConformancePass gates the later editions' LINE and RECORD SEQUENTIAL, ASSIGN USING, LOCK MODE, SHARING and COLLATING SEQUENCE (COBOL0900); all probed at --std 85, where an entry of all seven clauses written in reverse order with the minimum words also runs correctly. A second file-naming ASSIGN operand is refused (COBOL2256) under the implementor's rule that §1985:VII.2.3.3 SR3 allows, and the operand rules of the PADDING CHARACTER clause (an undefined data-name-1 compiles) are the rows of §1985:VII.2.7, held by kb/Work PB5070. The witness writes a three-clause entry and an OPTIONAL entry with six clauses in mixed order and checks the status values.

next.reason: §1985:VII.2.3.2, the sequential file control entry, offers SELECT [OPTIONAL], ASSIGN, RESERVE, [ORGANIZATION IS] SEQUENTIAL, PADDING CHARACTER, RECORD DELIMITER, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL and FILE STATUS. Its 2023 counterpart is 'Format 3 (sequential)' of §2023:12.4.5.1, which §2023:12.4.5.2 SR11 ('Format 3 shall be specified only for a sequential file or a report file') and §2023:12.4.5.3 GR8 ('The sequential format defines a file connector for a sequential file') tie to sequential files. It keeps every clause but PADDING CHARACTER, which no 2023 clause carries, so a 1985 entry with PADDING CHARACTER is refused; it also adds ASSIGN USING, LOCK MODE, SHARING and LINE/RECORD SEQUENTIAL. Narrower and wider at once, a compile-time difference with no exception condition: CHANGED. The order rule (§1985:VII.2.3.3 SR1) and each clause's own format carry their own records. Format 3 writes its clauses in line, and each is restated by its own clause format, so those state part of the entry's syntax too: §2023:12.4.5.5.1 (ACCESS MODE), §2023:12.4.5.8.2 (FILE STATUS), §2023:12.4.5.10.2 (ORGANIZATION), §2023:12.4.5.11.2 (RECORD DELIMITER), §2023:12.4.5.14.2 (RESERVE).
